claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has high density because it contains heavy elements, particularly Hf and Ta.
Slow cooling of Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr tends to produce brittle B2 or Laves phases.
Rapid solidification at cooling rates above approximately 10^5 K/s can induce or trap chemical short-range order in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr without forming long-range ordered or secondary phases.
Annealing below the SRO ordering temperature will stabilize the rapidly solidified SRO structure.
The relevant SRO in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr may consist of local arrangements such as Hf-Mo or Ta-Ti clustering.
In MoNbTaW, SRO hinders screw-dislocation motion while accelerating edge-dislocation motion.
In MoNbTaW, SRO increases the double-kink formation energy for screw dislocations.
In MoNbTaW, SRO flattens the energy landscape for edge dislocations, reducing solute drag.
SRO in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will increase room-temperature yield strength by impeding screw-dislocation motion.
SRO in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will preserve or improve fracture strain by facilitating edge-dislocation glide.
The opposing effects of SRO on screw and edge dislocations will enable high work hardening and strain accommodation.
Retaining a single-phase solid solution instead of heavy intermetallic precipitates will mitigate the alloy's density limitation.
The SRO-treated Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will remain single phase.
A conventionally cast random-solid-solution Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr baseline typically has low ductility because of brittle phase formation.
A conventionally cast Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr baseline may have low strength because it lacks ordering.
Evolution of SRO into B2 or Laves long-range order would embrittle Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
In MoNbTaW, the SRO strengthening effect is substantially diminished at 2000 K relative to 300 K because thermal entropy lowers the kink-pair nucleation barrier.
The useful temperature range for SRO strengthening in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr must remain below a corresponding thermal-disordering threshold.
Different elemental interactions in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr could produce phase separation or SRO configurations that do not accelerate edge dislocations.
APT and X-ray PDF analysis can distinguish samples with confirmed SRO from random-solid-solution controls and provide a Warren-Cowley SRO parameter.

contradictions.description: The density limitation is initially attributed to the elemental inventory, especially Hf and Ta, but is later claimed to be mitigated by suppressing intermetallic precipitates. At fixed composition, retaining a single phase does not by itself remove the density contribution of those heavy elements.

The baseline is described as a random solid solution, yet its low ductility is attributed to brittle B2 or Laves phase formation. A specimen containing substantial brittle secondary phases would not be a purely random single-phase solid solution.
